title: What First-Time Buyers Get Wrong About Their Budget
topic: What first time buyers get wrong about their budget
gbp_post:
The number first-time buyers focus on most is usually the one that matters least on its own. The purchase price gets all the attention, but it is rarely what surprises people at the closing table or six months into owning a home in South Tampa.

Property taxes here are based on assessed value, and in neighborhoods like Palma Ceia or Davis Islands, that number adjusts after a sale closes. The previous owner may have had a homestead exemption holding their tax bill down for years. Yours resets. The difference between what the listing showed and what you will actually owe can be several thousand dollars annually.

Then there is insurance. Flood zone designations vary block by block in South Tampa. A home on a quiet street off Bayshore might carry a flood policy that costs more than the homeowners policy itself. Neither number appears in the mortgage estimate your lender gives you at preapproval.

Closing costs run roughly two to five percent of the purchase price on top of the down payment. HOA fees, if the property has them, are monthly expenses that do not pause when something else breaks. And something always breaks within the first year.

Budgeting for the mortgage payment is the beginning, not the finish line. The buyers who feel most settled in their first year are the ones who treated the full picture as the real number before they ever made an offer.
